title: Press Kit Upload
description: A batch uploader where each thumbnail depixelates as its upload climbs — 2×2 blocks resolving to 4×4 to 8×8, then dissolving tile by tile against real progress — and the footer is a two-lane schedule rather than a bar: segments sized by how long each file takes, running ones swept and headed, queued ones hatched into the lane the scheduler predicts will free up first. Hover a lane segment and its row lights up. It opens mid-flight, and the video drops its connection at 61%.
intent: A real product surface with every state finished — queued, uploading, failed, retrying, done, empty, disabled — built on one mechanic (the preview resolving with the upload) on a flat light ground, which is the interface work Herb asked for over abstract demos.

changelog.summary:
1. **Depixelate instead of unblur** — dropped the CSS blur entirely. Each thumbnail's real content (gradient artwork, waveform silhouette, doc rules) is now sampled in JS into an 8×8 pixel grid, quantized into three levels — 2×2 → 4×4 → 8×8 — that snap forward as the upload climbs, then the 64 tiles dissolve one by one against actual progress in a deterministic scatter, so the image resolves out of blocks like a progressive load. Driven by one CSS variable on the parent (`opacity: clamp(0, calc((var(--udz-t) - var(--udz-p)) * 26), 1)`), so 512 tiles cost one attribute write per tick.

2. **Concurrency bar reinvented** — the aggregate progress bar is gone. In its place: a two-lane schedule, one lane per concurrent slot. Each file is a segment sized by how many seconds it takes, so the video visibly dominates; running segments carry a bright leading head and a sweeping accent sheen, done ones sit back at 30% accent as history, the failed one goes red, and queued files are hatched *ghost* segments dropped into whichever lane the scheduler predicts will free up first — a forecast that hardens as it runs. Hovering or tab-focusing a segment desaturates its siblings and lights the matchin
